description: Point-to-point gives each message to one consumer that shares the work; publish/subscribe gives every subscriber its own copy.
A received message stays in the queue but hidden; if it is not acknowledged before the timeout, it becomes visible and is redelivered.
Where a message goes after too many failed deliveries, so a poison message stops wasting deliveries and someone can inspect it.
A Kafka topic is split into append-only logs; each message has an increasing offset, and consumers commit the offset they processed.
Consumers that share a topic: each partition is read by one member at a time, while separate groups each read every message.
Process first, acknowledge after: a crash in between means the message arrives again, so duplicates are expected.
Records the id of every processed message, ideally in the same transaction as the effect, and skips ids it has already seen.
How far consumers are behind producers: offsets not yet processed in a log, or the count and age of waiting messages in a queue.
